menu.description: Health of the ERP integration, sync log, reset and controls
menu.label: Integration

gridColumns.description: The ERP's order number and whether the order reached the ERP
gridColumns.label: ERP order

schema.description: Orders placed on this website are created in the ERP, and the ERP's order number is written back.
schema.label: Send orders to the ERP
schema.name: orders_send

schema.description: An order placed while the ERP is offline is sent when the ERP is back (retried for up to a day). When off, such an order is not sent.
schema.label: Hold orders while the ERP is offline
schema.name: orders_hold_offline

schema.description: A status code to set on the Commerce order when the ERP confirms it, created at Stores → Settings → Order Status and assigned to the Pending state (not as its default), for example erp_confirmed. Blank: a note only. No status can move an order to Processing; Commerce does that itself when the order is invoiced or shipped.
schema.label: Order status when the ERP confirms
schema.name: orders_confirm_status

schema.description: The ERP sales organization that sells through this website (four letters or digits, like an SAP sales org). Orders from this website carry it.
schema.label: ERP sales organization for this website
schema.name: structure_sales_org

schema.description: What the ERP calls that sales organization. Blank: the ERP prints the website's name.
schema.label: Sales organization name
schema.name: structure_sales_org_name

schema.description: Put in front of the ERP order number written onto Commerce orders, as ACME-0000001042, so two ERPs on one store tell their orders apart. Blank: the first four letters of the ERP's name. Set at Default Config.
schema.label: Prefix on ERP order numbers in Commerce
schema.name: structure_order_prefix

schema.description: Which products belong to this ERP. All: every product (one ERP). Inventory sources: the products stocked in the sources named below. Attribute: the products whose attribute names this ERP. Set at Default Config.
schema.label: Which products belong to this ERP
schema.name: structure_owns

options.label: Products in the inventory sources named below
Products whose attribute names this ERP

schema.description: Comma-separated inventory source codes this ERP ships from (used with Inventory sources above).
schema.label: Inventory sources this ERP ships from
schema.name: structure_owns_sources

schema.description: A product attribute and value that names this ERP, as erp_owner=ACME (used with Attribute above).
schema.label: Product attribute that names this ERP
schema.name: structure_owns_attribute

schema.description: The timezone the schedules below are read in, as an IANA name like America/Chicago or Europe/Berlin. Set at Default Config.
schema.label: Store timezone for schedules
schema.name: schedule_timezone

schema.description: Publish each ERP's prices in force into the companies' shared catalogs on the schedule below, so a price whose start or end date arrives takes effect. Set at Default Config.
schema.label: Publish ERP prices into the shared catalogs
schema.name: schedule_prices_enabled

schema.description: How often the price publish runs.
schema.label: Price publish: how often
schema.name: schedule_prices_frequency

schema.description: The minute past each hour, store time, the hourly price publish runs at.
schema.label: Price publish: minute past the hour
schema.name: schedule_prices_minute

schema.description: The time of day, store time, as HH:MM in 24 hours, the daily or weekly price publish runs at. It runs within five minutes of it.
schema.label: Price publish: time of day
schema.name: schedule_prices_time

schema.description: The day the weekly price publish runs on.
schema.label: Price publish: day of the week
schema.name: schedule_prices_weekday

events.description: Fires after a product is created or updated in Commerce, used to keep the ERP materials in step between resets
events.label: Product Created or Updated
events.name: observer.catalog_product_save_commit_after

events.description: Fires after a product is deleted in Commerce, so the ERP copy goes too instead of lingering until the next reset
events.label: Product Deleted
events.name: observer.catalog_product_delete_commit_after

events.description: Fires after a B2B company is created or changed in Commerce, so the business partner in the ERP follows at once (it replaces the minute refresh that polled every company)
events.label: Company Saved
events.name: observer.company_save_commit_after

events.description: Fires after an order is saved in Commerce, used to create each new order in the ERP and write back the ERP order number
events.label: Order Saved
events.name: observer.sales_order_save_commit_after

events.description: Fires after a shipment is saved in Commerce, so a shipment made in Commerce Admin is recorded on the ERP order
events.label: Shipment Saved
events.name: observer.sales_order_shipment_save_after

events.description: Fires after an invoice is saved in Commerce, so an invoice made in Commerce Admin invoices the ERP order
events.label: Invoice Saved
events.name: observer.sales_order_invoice_save_after

events.description: Fires after a return is saved in Commerce, so each ERP that sold its lines is sent its return order (the return itself is read from Commerce)
events.label: Return Saved
events.name: observer.rma_save_commit_after

events.description: Fires after a stock item is saved in Commerce, used to keep the ERP stock in step with the store
events.label: Stock Item Updated
events.name: observer.cataloginventory_stock_item_save_commit_after

provider.description: Commerce events the ERP integration listens to
provider.label: Commerce Provider

events.description: The ERP changed a product price or name
events.label: ERP Product Updated
events.name: be-observer.catalog_product_update

events.description: The ERP changed stock levels
events.label: ERP Stock Updated
events.name: be-observer.catalog_stock_update

events.description: The ERP confirmed a sales order
events.label: ERP Order Status Updated
events.name: be-observer.sales_order_status_update

events.description: The ERP shipped a sales order
events.label: ERP Order Shipment Created
events.name: be-observer.sales_order_shipment_create

events.description: The ERP invoiced a sales order
events.label: ERP Order Invoice Created
events.name: be-observer.sales_order_invoice_create

events.description: The ERP cancelled a sales order
events.label: ERP Order Cancelled
events.name: be-observer.sales_order_cancel

events.description: The ERP put a sales order on credit hold, or released it
events.label: ERP Order Credit Hold
events.name: be-observer.sales_order_hold

events.description: The ERP posted a credit memo for some lines of a sales order, for a return or without one
events.label: ERP Order Credit Memo Created
events.name: be-observer.sales_order_creditmemo_create

events.description: The ERP posted a payment against an invoice of a sales order
events.label: ERP Order Payment Received
events.name: be-observer.sales_order_payment_create

events.description: The goods of a return order are back in the ERP warehouse
events.label: ERP Return Received
events.name: be-observer.rma_status_update

events.description: The ERP changed an account credit limit
events.label: ERP Company Credit Updated
events.name: be-observer.company_credit_update

events.description: The ERP blocked or unblocked an account
events.label: ERP Company Status Updated
events.name: be-observer.company_status_update

events.description: The ERP changed the prices in force for a customer (its price lists), sent as the whole set for that customer
events.label: ERP Customer Prices Updated
events.name: be-observer.company_contract_update

provider.description: The ERP, the back-office system that publishes these events
provider.label: ERP Provider

customInstallationSteps.description: Names this app's Commerce event provider in Commerce's eventing configuration, which the installer leaves blank.
customInstallationSteps.name: Set the event provider id

metadata.description: Adobe Commerce integration to a demo ERP: orders to the ERP with the ERP number written back, the ERP's contract prices in each company's shared catalog, and the ERP events (prices, stock, credit limits, order statuses) applied to Commerce.

webhooks.description: As the order is placed, asks each owning ERP whether the company can carry its part (credit) and by when it can promise the quantity (availability); a definitive credit refusal stops the order, a slow or down ERP never does
webhooks.label: ERP credit and availability at placement

webhook.fallback_error_message: The ERP could not confirm this order right now. Please try again in a moment.
